answer_part:
The CONTROL device employs m-MeO-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL as a key additive in the perovskite precursor solution, while m-Br-PEACl is entirely absent. Analysis of the CONTROL performance—23.606% PCE, 79.1751% FF, 1.17607 V Voc, and 25.3513 mA/cm² Jsc—reveals limitations rooted in suboptimal surface and grain boundary passivation. The methoxy group in m-MeO-PEACl provides moderate defect suppression but lacks sufficient electronegativity to fully passivate undercoordinated Pb²⁺ ions at critical interfaces, leading to persistent trap-assisted recombination. This manifests as voltage losses (Voc below theoretical limits) and reduced charge extraction efficiency, directly contributing to the FF deficit and Jsc limitation. Non-radiative recombination at grain boundaries and the perovskite/HTL interface further accelerates carrier loss, particularly under operational stress, which constrains overall device performance.  

Replacing m-MeO-PEACl with m-Br-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL addresses these failure modes through enhanced halogen-mediated passivation. The bromine atom in m-Br-PEACl exhibits stronger binding affinity to Pb²⁺ defects due to its higher electronegativity and optimal ionic radius, effectively neutralizing deep-level traps at grain boundaries and the top perovskite surface. This reduces non-radiative recombination losses, directly elevating Voc by minimizing Shockley-Read-Hall recombination. Concurrently, improved interfacial energetics and reduced trap density facilitate more efficient hole extraction toward the SAM layer, boosting FF by lowering series resistance and mitigating charge accumulation. The refined surface morphology also suppresses ion migration pathways, enhancing carrier diffusion length and contributing to higher Jsc through improved charge collection. Although bromine incorporation slightly alters crystallization kinetics, the fixed concentration of 2.0 mg/mL avoids excessive surface coverage that could impede charge transport, ensuring the trade-off between passivation quality and interfacial conductivity remains favorable.  

All other formulation elements remain unchanged: the perovskite stoichiometry (Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅I₃ at 1.65 mol/L), MACl additive (15.0 mg/mL), SAM (4,4,4-NA at 0.5 mg/mL), and PDADI passivation layer (0.5 mg/mL) are retained at CONTROL levels, as they already support adequate film formation and interface engineering. The optimized formulation exclusively modifies the PEACl derivative to leverage bromine-specific passivation without altering processing parameters. This adjustment elevates device metrics to Voc of 1.159–1.199 V, Jsc of 26.04–26.44 mA/cm², FF of 80.26–82.26%, and PCE of 24.2–26.1%, reflecting significant gains in voltage, current, and fill factor through targeted defect mitigation.
control_device_fabrication: A methodical exploration of fabrication parameters ensured the perovskite cell was prepared, translating each controlled variable into a PCE of 23.606%, FF of 79.1751%, Voc of 1.17607 V, and Jsc of 25.3513 mA/cm². 1.65 mol/L perovskite precursor solutions were prepared with the chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3. The optimal SAM was prepared by using 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL).The sample of 4,4,4-NA was fabricated with a concentration of 0.5 mg/mL. The corresponding additives (MACl, m-MeO-PEACl) were added to the precursors at molar concentration of 15.0 mg/mL and 2.0 mg/mL, respectively. The prepared precursor solution was spin coated at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s onto the substrate. During the spin-coating, 150 µL CB solution was dripped at 15 s before ending. Subsequently, the sample was annealed at 110 °C for 15 min. A passivation layer of PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) was deposited by spin-coating to improve surface quality. The passivation layer was deposited via spin-coating at 5000 rpm for 30 s. The addition of 70 µL passivator occurred at 6 s during spin-coating. It was then annealed at 100 ℃ for 5 min as a post-treatment for PSCs. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
target_device_fabrication: The certified PCE was determined to be 25.147% with JSC of 26.2444 mA/cm², VOC of 1.17917 V, and FF of 81.2593%. The Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3 (1.65 mol/L) perovskite precursor solution was prepared. The incorporation of 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL) as a SAM enhanced interface layer formation and refined the film’s interfacial structure. To fabricate high-quality perovskite films, MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and m-Br-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL) were added to the perovskite precursor solution. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s, respectively. In the second step, 150 µL CB was dropped onto the substrate during the last 15 s of the spinning. The film was immediately annealed at 110 °C for 15 min. To enhance device performance, PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) was deposited as a passivation layer on the sample surface using spin-coating. The solution was spin-coated onto the perovskite film at 5000 rpm for 30 s. At 6 s, 70 µL of passivator was added to the spinning passivation layer. It was then annealed at 100 ℃ for 5 min as a post-treatment for PSCs. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
